newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Franc retreat prompts Paris stock surge.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Franc retreat prompts Paris stock surge.

text.p: French shares surged almost one percent on Thursday after the franc came under pressure following comments from a Bank of France policymaker.
Bank of France monetary policy council member Jean-Pierre Gerard said in an interview with Le Monde he wanted a stronger dollar against the mark, implying a desire for a weaker franc.
One way to get the dollar higher would be to cut short-term rates in France and Germany.

"Unfortunately we have little influence on German monetary policy," he was quoted as saying. "A second possibility, given that we cannot get a concerted reduction in rates, would be to modify the franc-mark parity."
Economists said they doubted the French would embark on a different monetary policy.
"France would clearly like a stronger dollar. I suspect Germany would not have a problem with that," said Ian Harwood, international economist at Kleinwort Benson.
Harwood said comments by the BOF's Gerard illustrate there is a growing rift within France about the franc fort policy.
Around midday, the franc stood at 3.3940 per mark compared with 3.3860 late on Wednesday and at 5.2027 against the dollar, compared with 5.1725.
French shares rose smartly as the franc slid and were up more than 0.95 percent on hopes that the weaker currency could lead to lower interest rates, traders said.
But they remained worried over the French truck drivers' strike, now into 11th day, which could upset investment sentiment as workers face further temporary layoffs due to supply problems.
German shares also received an early lift when the dollar raced up to its highest level for a month against the mark, boosting German exporting stocks in particular.

The DAX index of 30 leading shares touched a day's high of 2,818.65 points, just below its all-time record high of 2,819.95 points, and was up more than 0.7 percent at midday, but business was dampened by Thanksgiving holiday in United States..
The dollar penetrated the 1.53 mark level, after the Gerard's comments.

Shares in Europe's biggest carmaker Volkswagen AG recovered after a newspaper report that its production chief Jose Ignacio Lopez de Arriortua was likely to offer his resignation. Sources close to the company said he was expected to resign from his post on Friday.
Lopez is at the centre of a VW legal battle with Opel, a unit of U.S. giant General Motors, over alleged industrial espionage charges.
In London at midday the FTSE 100 index of top shares was down 0.2 percent, with confidence damped by losses on Wall Street overnight.
"The Dow has been one of the main crutches of our support recently and after the run-up to the Budget the profit-taking will probably continue today," another trader said.
A sharp 100 point advance in the FTSE to record levels in the two pre-Budget sessions was halted on Wednesday when some said the rise had been overdone.
"We went up too far too quickly," a trader said. "I wouldn't be surprised to see us heading straight back down to 4,000."

The dollar pushed higher against the yen in Europe and dealers said the reason was the Bank of Japan's uninspiring quarterly Tankan report of business confidence on Wednesday. "It is a carry-over from the tankan report, which was weaker than expected, and the belief that (Japanese) rates will not rise," said a senior dealer at a British bank.

In metals, Copper prices rose above $2,300 a tonne, the highest since the Sumitomo Corp scandal erupted in June, as critically low inventory levels forced buyers to scramble for metal, traders and analysts said.
But gold was fixed at $372.20, its lowest fix in over 2-1/2 years, as soaring stock markets and the stronger dollar pulled investor money out of bullion.

Oil prices held firm on news OPEC oil ministers had agreed to a new six-month freeze of their oil output quotas at 25.03 million barrels a day. Benchmark North Sea Brent Blend crude was trading just below $22.90 a barrel.
CURRENCIES at 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.63 yen and 1.5328 marks against 113.33 yen and 1.5275 marks in late Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was down 10.4 points at 4,038.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 22.02 at 2,292.79.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 20.30 at 2817.78.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $372.20 against $373.00 previously, the lowest fix since April 25, 1994. Silver was unchanged at $4.74, while platinum fixed $1.50 down at $374.75.
